# Today on Hacker News

## 🤖 AI & Machine Learning

The AI conversation dominates today's front page. **"Notes from the Mistral AI Now Summit"** offers a firsthand look at the latest developments from one of Europe's leading AI labs, while **"Liquid AI reveals 8B-A1B MoE trained on 38T"** highlights a new Mixture-of-Experts model trained on a staggering 38 trillion tokens — a sign of just how fast the frontier is moving. On the tooling side, **"Show HN: Tiny-vLLM – high performance LLM inference engine in C++ and CUDA"** showcases community-driven work to make LLM inference faster and leaner. More provocatively, **"MCP Is Dead"** questions the longevity of the Model Context Protocol, and **"Shift will clean homes for free to train future robots"** raises eyebrows about the lengths companies will go to gather real-world training data. Rounding out the theme, **"Is AI causing a repeat of frontend's lost decade?"** sparks a lively debate about whether AI-generated code is quietly degrading the quality of web development.

---

## 💻 Programming & Developer Tools

Several high-scoring posts speak directly to the craft of software engineering. **"SQLite is all you need for durable workflows"** (307 points) makes a compelling case for leaning on SQLite as a reliable backbone for stateful, long-running processes — a counterpoint to heavyweight orchestration systems. **"Bijou64: A variable-length integer encoding"** from Ink & Switch dives into the elegant design of a compact integer format, while **"On Rendering Diffs"** explores the surprisingly nuanced problem of displaying code differences clearly and intuitively. **"You can just say it"**, penned by Redis creator antirez, offers a philosophical nudge toward plain, direct communication in technical writing.

---

## 🖥️ Hardware & Gadgets

Hardware enthusiasts have plenty to chew on. **"It's hard to justify buying a Framework 12"** (200 points) is a candid review from Jeff Geerling arguing that the latest modular laptop, while admirable in principle, struggles to compete on pure value. Meanwhile, **"Print with dozens of colors: Our new open-source ColorMix for PrusaSlicer"** announces an exciting multi-color 3D printing feature from Prusa, lowering the bar for vibrant, complex prints at home.

---

## 🌐 Society, Economics & Policy

The most-discussed post of the day is **"The dead economy theory"** (613 points, 799 comments), a thought-provoking essay arguing that large swaths of modern economic activity are hollow or self-referential. On the policy front, **"The California state assembly has passed the 'Protect Our Games Act'"** is a win for the Stop Killing Games movement, requiring publishers to keep games playable even after official support ends — a landmark moment for digital consumer rights. Finally, **"Free full BGP feed. IPv4 and IPv6"** is a quiet but useful resource for network engineers needing full internet routing tables for lab work.
